source_quote: But if you are a global enterprise, you are dealing with thousands of concepts. You can't just have all these entities thrown into one massive bucket, it would be chaos. Total chaos. Which is why the system relies heavily on namespaces and inheritance. Namespaces act as organizational boundaries or scopes for your definitions. So the HR department's definition of a contract, which might mean an employment agreement, doesn't collide and override the sales department's definition of a contract, which means a customer purchase agreement. Exactly. Namespaces prevent those semantic collisions,
